title: Rename a theme
prompt:
# Story 2: Rename a theme

- **Story**: XXX-rename-theme
- **Created**: 2026-11-15
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: double-click `checkout-flow`, type "  Cobrança Online  " and Enter to get `cobranca-online`; press F2 and try "2024-goals", an
  empty name and the name of another theme; rename a theme that holds the open story and see its path change.

## Story

As a team member, I want to rename a theme when I find a better name for it, so that the name says what its stories have in common, without
moving every story by hand.

## Acceptance tests

Starting and ending a rename

- [ ] **Given** a theme, **When** the user double-clicks it, **Then** its name becomes an edit field with the whole text selected, and the
  folder is open or closed as it was before the double-click.
- [ ] **Given** a theme has the focus, **When** the user presses F2, **Then** its name becomes an edit field, as with a double-click.
- [ ] **Given** a theme row, **When** the pointer rests on it, **Then** the tooltip reads "Click twice (or press F2) to rename".
- [ ] **Given** the edit field, **When** the user presses Enter, or leaves the field, **Then** the new name is saved. **When** the user
  presses Escape, **Then** nothing changes.
- [ ] **Given** the edit field, **When** the user keeps the same name and presses Enter, **Then** nothing changes and the field closes.
- [ ] **Given** a story folder, the `stories` folder, another folder or a file, **When** the user double-clicks it or presses F2, **Then**
  nothing is renamed.

The name

- [ ] **Given** the user types "  Cobrança Online  ", **Then** the theme is named `cobranca-online`: the spaces around are removed, the words
  are lower case and joined by "-", and the accents are removed. Any other sign also becomes a "-".
- [ ] **Given** the user clears the name, or types only spaces or signs, **When** Enter, **Then** "Give the theme a name." shows under the
  field, the field stays open, and nothing is saved.
- [ ] **Given** the user types "2024-goals", **When** Enter, **Then** "A theme name starts with a letter." shows and nothing is saved.
- [ ] **Given** a theme `checkout-flow` exists, **When** another is renamed "Checkout Flow", **Then** "A theme with this name already
  exists." shows and nothing is saved.
- [ ] **Given** a message under the field, **When** the user types again, **Then** the message goes away.
- [ ] **Given** a name that is not good, **When** the user leaves the field, **Then** the theme goes back to its old name, and no message
  stays.
- [ ] **Given** the user types a name longer than 40 characters, **Then** it is cut to 40 characters, with no "-" at the end.

What moves with it

- [ ] **Given** a theme `checkout-flow` with the stories `003-checkout-form` and `007-pay-by-card`, **When** it is renamed `payments`,
  **Then** both story folders are inside `payments`, and their identities, texts, statuses, links, tasks, diagrams and UI examples are as
  they were.
- [ ] **Given** the open story is in the theme, **When** the theme is renamed, **Then** the story stays open, with the path
  `stories/payments/003-checkout-form/story.md`.
- [ ] **Given** the theme was open, **When** it is renamed, **Then** it is still open under its new name, in its new place in the
  alphabetical order.
- [ ] **Given** the theme has a saved runway (story 5), **When** it is renamed, **Then** the runway belongs to the theme under its new name.

## Business rules and constraints

- **Keeping its own name is allowed.** The check that a name is taken leaves out the theme being renamed.
- **A rename is not an edit of a story.** It does not change the text or the status of any story.
- **In the repository, each story moves when it is synchronised** (story 4). A rename does not open a pull request on its own.

## Out of scope

- Undoing a rename.
- Renaming story folders, the `stories` folder or files from the tree.
- Synchronising every story of a renamed theme in one pull request.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add the rename to the theme row: double-click and F2 open the name field of story 1 with the current name.
- [ ] Rename in the data: the theme in the list, the theme of each of its stories, and its saved runway.
- [ ] Keep the theme open under its new name.
- [ ] Test the rename of a theme with two stories, one of them open, and the messages.

tasks.text: Add double-click and F2 handlers to the theme row component that open an inline name field pre-filled with the current name and fully selected (Architecture: UI layer)
Add a tooltip `"Click twice (or press F2) to rename"` to the theme row (Architecture: UI layer)
Implement the slug-transformation function (trim, lower-case, strip diacritics, non-alphanumeric → `-`, collapse, truncate to 40) in the entities layer and unit-test it (Architecture: entities layer)
Implement validation rules (non-empty after transformation, must start with a letter, must be unique excluding self) in the use-case layer and unit-test each rule (Architecture: use-cases layer)

Implement a `RenameThemeViewModel` that holds edit state, exposes the validation message, and calls the rename use case; unit-test it with a test double for the use case (Architecture: interface-adapters layer, ADR-0007)
Wire the rename use case: update the theme name in the project state, reassign the theme field of every story in that theme, and update the runway association (Architecture: use-cases layer)
Update the tree to keep the renamed theme open and re-sort it alphabetically after the rename (Architecture: UI layer)
Update the open-story path display when the story's theme is renamed (Architecture: UI layer)

Write a Jest integration test covering: rename `checkout-flow` to `payments` with two stories (one open), verify story contents are unchanged, the open story path updates, the theme is open in its new alphabetical position, and the runway is reassigned (Practice: Pair programming, ADR-0005)
Write Jest tests for each validation message and for the blur-reverts-to-old-name behaviour (Practice: Pair programming)
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build)
